label: r4c2
name: r3c1 with 32 minibatches
hypothesis: Same as r3c1, but n_minibatches is 32 instead of 16. This doubles the gradient steps per update (64 instead of 32) with smaller minibatches, at the same sample budget and compute. Training is limited by optimisation speed, so more steps per batch should help, as the higher lr did. Refuted if dev success is at most about 0.85.
last_analysis: Mirroring the trunk features (flip-concat) and pooling them over each brick footprint is what lets the agent learn this world at all. Without it, or with a learned column remap (0.40), results are much weaker. The recipe matters a lot. Two PPO epochs gave 0.72, against 0.53 with four. One epoch collapsed into ending every episode with DONE straight away (0.00). Raising lr to 0.002 gave the best result, 0.89, with both seeds close together. A larger network costs samples and lost: a deeper trunk scored 0.56 and a wider head 0.48. A longer gamma made seeds unstable (0.30). The global-context head (0.76 vs 0.72) is within noise. r3c1's training curve was still rising at the end (0.72 to 0.83), so the agent is still limited by optimisation speed at this budget. In this final round I keep the r3c1 network and push optimisation speed: lr 0.003, more minibatch steps per update, and the global-context head combined with lr 0.002.
